Treasury
TREZH-uh-ree
noun
From the Latin thesaurus, “a store, hoard,” through the Old French tresorie; a place where wealth or sacred offerings are stored.

📖 Biblical Definition

A treasury is the place where wealth, tribute, or the offerings of God’s house are stored and kept. Under the old covenant the spoil of Jericho, the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron, was consecrated and brought “into the treasury of the house of the LORD” (Jos 6:19, 24). In the temple of the second covenant stood the treasury where the people cast their offerings, and there our Lord sat and watched: “Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much” (Mar 12:41). Then came a poor widow who threw in two mites, which make a farthing; and the Lord called His disciples and said that she had cast in more than they all, “for all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living” (Mar 12:44; Luk 21:1–4). When the chief priests took the betrayal-money Judas flung down, they said it was not lawful to put it “into the treasury, because it is the price of blood” (Mat 27:6), scrupling over the vessel while plotting murder. The treasury thus becomes a place of searching judgment, where God weighs not the amount but the heart of the giver. The widow’s two mites, weighed in the treasury of heaven, outshine the rich man’s heaped abundance, for the LORD measures the gift by the love and the sacrifice from which it flows.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A place where wealth or sacred offerings are stored; the temple treasury where the widow cast her two mites.

TREASURY, a place where wealth or offerings are stored and kept.

The spoil of Jericho was brought into the treasury of the LORD (Jos 6:24).

Jesus sat over against the temple treasury and watched the givers (Mar 12:41).

A poor widow cast in two mites, all her living (Mar 12:44).

The priests would not put the price of blood into the treasury (Mat 27:6).

📖 Key Scripture

Mar 12:41 — "And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much."

Mar 12:44 — "For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living."

Luk 21:1 — "And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury."

Mat 27:6 — "And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; the treasury witnesses that God weighs the heart of the giver, not the amount of the gift.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson to recover is that God weighs not the amount of a gift but the heart from which it flows. Christ sat over against the treasury and watched; the rich cast in much of their abundance, but the poor widow cast in two mites of her want, and the Lord judged that she had given more than all the rest, for she gave all her living. In the treasury of heaven the smallest gift offered in faith and love outweighs the largest given out of surplus and self.

The treasury also rebukes a religion that is scrupulous about outward forms while harbouring inward corruption. The chief priests would not defile the treasury with the price of blood, yet they had paid that price to betray innocent blood, straining at a gnat and swallowing a camel. So the treasury searches the giver: it exposes both the widow’s costly love and the hypocrite’s hollow nicety. What a man does with his substance before the eye of God is a true gauge of his heart, for where his treasure is, there will his heart be also.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word comes from thesaurus, a store or hoard, naming the place where wealth and offerings are kept.

Treasury — Latin thesaurus, “a store” or “hoard.”

It is the place where wealth or offerings are kept.

The spoil of Jericho was brought into the LORD’s treasury.

Jesus watched the givers at the temple treasury.

The widow’s two mites outweighed the rich man’s abundance.

"Like the widow at the treasury, the smallest gift of love outweighs the largest given of surplus."

"The treasury teaches that God weighs the heart of the giver, not the amount of the gift."

"What a man does with his substance before God’s eye is a true gauge of his heart."
